overall: Atlanta reached a running max of 95.0°F around 13:25 ET before a sharp convective outflow dropped temperatures dramatically to 87.8°F with winds surging to 23 mph by 13:52 ET — a classic storm outflow signature consistent with the active Severe Thunderstorm Warning and Special Weather Statements. The day started strong thermally but has been interrupted by active convection, with the 30-minute velocity of -10.8°F/hr signaling a significant and abrupt cooling event rather than typical afternoon tapering.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show considerable spread (NBM=93.6°F to GFS=98.1°F), and observed temperatures are tracking near the lower-to-middle end of that range. The HRRR at 95.2°F aligns most closely with what's been observed, while GFS and ECMWF appear too warm given the convective disruption now underway. The intraday obs-driven model has sharply downgraded probabilities above 98°F to near zero, diverging substantially from the META and D1_NOW models that haven't fully ingested the storm impact.
max_temp_prediction: The 95.0°F running max set at 13:25 ET is the most likely candidate for today's TMAX. While some partial temperature recovery is possible after the storm passes, the severity of the outflow cooling (~7°F drop in under 30 minutes), the lateness of the afternoon, and continued storm activity in the region make it unlikely that temperatures will climb back above 95°F to challenge the 96-97°F even-bucket market leader. The active even-bucket ensemble (96-97F @ 28.3%, Tier 2) may overstate upside risk given the storm disruption; the intraday model's 94-95F at 39.0% better reflects current ground truth, though a finish right at 95°F bridges both buckets.
